12	===== BRIEF.md
13	# Asset brief
14	
15	Create coherent pixel-art status assets for the queue UI. Preserve the existing vector Start control. Status cells are 16 by 16 logical pixels. Working uses four horizontal frames with a 100 ms frame duration. Ready and Retry are static images. Use transparent backgrounds, readable silhouettes and the existing UI's cool blue accent; a fixed palette is not required. Inspect at 1x and 3x nearest display scale on the actual dark panel. The working loop must communicate activity without looking like success. Error/retry must be distinguishable without color alone.
16	
17	Assets belong at the paths already used by the view. Account badges are provided by a server registry and are outside this local asset request. No approved style reference exists yet: propose a representative status sample before expanding the family.
18	
19	Update: the queue now supports a paused state. Its status image must be distinguishable from activity, completion and retry without relying on color alone. Keep the existing style and display requirements. The failure visual moved to the path in the updated view; its purpose is unchanged.
20	
21	Current update: Ready must visibly use a check mark with asymmetrical arms to convey successful completion. The destination now follows the updated view. Keep the existing 16x16 canvas, static behavior, transparent background and review display conditions.

export type QueueState = "idle" | "running" | "succeeded" | "failed" | "paused";
export function stateAfter(result: "started" | "ok" | "error" | "pause"): QueueState {
  return { started: "running", ok: "succeeded", error: "failed", pause: "paused" }[result] as QueueState;
}

===== src/queue-view.ts
import type { QueueState } from "./queue";
export const statusVisuals = {
  idle: { label: "Start", path: "assets/start.svg", frames: 1 },
  running: { label: "Working", path: "assets/working.png", frames: 4 },
  paused: { label: "Paused", path: "assets/paused.png", frames: 1 },
  succeeded: { label: "Ready", path: "assets/ready-confirmed.png", frames: 1 },
  failed: { label: "Retry", path: "assets/error-retry.png", frames: 1 },
};
export const display = { cell: [16, 16], scale: 3, filter: "nearest", frameMs: 100, background: "#172336" };
export function statusCell(state: QueueState) { return statusVisuals[state]; }
export function compactStatus(state: QueueState) { return statusVisuals[state]; }
export function accountBadge(registry: Record<string, string>, account: string) {
  return registry[account]; // Provided by the service; not enumerable in this checkout.
}

// Execute the actual source consumers; this is not a renderer.
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import { stateAfter } from './src/queue.ts';
import { statusCell, compactStatus, display } from './src/queue-view.ts';
const expected = process.argv[2];
assert.ok(expected, 'Pass the selected PLAR delivery path');
const state = stateAfter('ok');
assert.equal(state, 'succeeded');
const consumers = [statusCell(state), compactStatus(state)];
for (const consumer of consumers) {
  assert.equal(consumer.path, expected);
  assert.equal(consumer.frames, 1);
}
const data = readFileSync(new URL(expected, import.meta.url));
assert.equal(data.subarray(0,8).toString('hex'), '89504e470d0a1a0a');
assert.deepEqual([data.readUInt32BE(16), data.readUInt32BE(20)], display.cell);
assert.equal(display.filter, 'nearest');
const hash = bytes => createHash('sha256').update(bytes).digest('hex');
console.log(JSON.stringify({state, consumers, display, file: expected,
  sha256: hash(data), sources: Object.fromEntries(['src/queue.ts','src/queue-view.ts'].map(
    p => [p, hash(readFileSync(new URL(p, import.meta.url)))])),
  scope: 'Executed backend-to-view mapping and actual file/header lookup; no renderer, alpha compositing or artistic acceptance.'}, null, 2));

requirements.name: transparent-background

The specialist returns exact source/request/criteria artifacts; the caller reads them independently and records a source-grounded comparison. - `checks`: actual mechanical, visual and integration findings, with evidence paths and unavailable checks.

An assignment ending at an accepted request is delivered when that request and its resumable state are returned, while the asset remains unaccepted and its production task open. 1	# Request and criteria handoff
2	
3	Use for delegated asset work when a proposed production contract is ready to adopt, or when its consequential request/criteria change. The specialist prepares the contract; the calling agent independently compares its actual contents to the original assignment. This is an agent-to-agent review, not a new user-approval gate. Continue under established authorization when the contract is consistent.
4	
5	## Specialist: return the exact proposed contract
6	
7	Save a compact `request-review.json` in the consumer project. Point to existing artifacts instead of duplicating provider history or manufacturing PX2 state for a planning-only task. Its fields are:
8	
9	- `version`: 1.
10	- `sources`: the brief and relevant consumer/reference sources, each with project-relative `path`, actual byte `sha256`, and `role`; include locators for the adopted decisions. Numbered locators refer to that individual file, never a concatenated multi-file terminal display. The caller verifies the cited content at those locators. Include the selected `requirements_hash` when PLAR supplied one.
11	- `request`: `path`, `sha256`, `kind` (`provider_arguments` or `creative_brief`) and the actual tool name when known. Provider arguments must be the complete exact JSON to dispatch, including real reference inputs. Use a creative brief when an operation/schema has not been discovered; do not label it executable.
12	- `criteria`: `path` and `sha256` for the exact criteria to use. Each criterion has an ID, check, authority/basis, applicable scope and source locator. Distinguish owner/consumer requirements, specialist sample choices, observations and diagnostics.
13	- `choices`: the consequential specialist choices or unresolved decisions, where each appears in the request/criteria, and its reason. A criterion scoped to a chosen sample can assess that sample; it does not establish a universal project requirement.
14	- `resume`: existing store/task/output/job links when applicable. Omit absent production state.
15	
16	Return the packet's path and SHA-256 to the caller. For PX2 production, link the saved request and Q records or an exact exported view with their state/record identity. Do not silently rebuild the request after review. Before dispatch, compare the actual arguments to the reviewed request; reference bytes/handles and non-text controls matter as much as prompt wording.
17	
18	Keep a required outcome separate from the recipe proposed to achieve it. A qualitative requirement such as matching a reference or conveying a state still needs an acceptance criterion when its palette, geometry, frame count or layout are open. When demoting an unsupported recipe to a sample choice, preserve the underlying required outcome; do not leave only mechanical checks binding. Consumer code establishes its actual data/rendering behavior, not an unmeasured aesthetic quality. Attribute expert quality criteria to expert judgment where that is their basis.
19	
20	Creative decisions within the assignment need not all go back to the user. For example, choosing a static first sample or a construction method is expert judgment; attributing it to an owner who specified only canvas dimensions is incorrect. Keep the choice explicit and scoped so it can be revised without changing the owner's brief. Observations alone do not become rejection rules.
21	
22	### Measured facts in creative requests
23	
24	Do not estimate pixel coordinates by eye and then describe them as verified. When a numerical image fact materially guides a request or verdict, retain the measurement with its source-image hash, frame and coordinate convention. The existing `asset-check --regions COLOR...` / `pixl_asset_check(regions=[...])` measures exact RGBA component boxes; it does not identify the subject or make those colors mandatory. Boxes use zero-based coordinates with exclusive right/bottom edges. For other measurements, save the reproducible calculation. When exact coordinates are unnecessary, describe the visual relationship and supply the actual reference instead.
25	
26	The caller independently verifies consequential measured claims against the original image and measurement, including the coordinate convention; repeating a specialist's pixel map is not independent verification. Correct unsupported numbers before dispatch while preserving the required visual outcome.
27	
28	## Resolve source evidence for the comparison
29	
30	For candidate plans used by selected-asset preparation, call `pixl_request_review`
31	with the packet path and selected `asset_id` (CLI `request-review PACKET --asset ID
32	--root PROJECT`). It reads the exact request/criteria identities, returns cited text
33	with file-local bounds, and includes the current production continuation. It reports
34	invalid/unresolved locators and changed sources. A resolved excerpt is evidence for
35	the caller to interpret, not a consistency verdict. Retain this report with the review.
36	
37	When the connection is already discovered, bind `request.provider` and
38	`request.connection: {path, sha256}` to its exact artifact. Preparation compares that
39	reviewed connection with the supplied one; host credentials stay outside the artifact.

# Request and criteria handoff

Use for delegated asset work when a proposed production contract is ready to adopt, or when its consequential request/criteria change. The specialist prepares the contract; the calling agent independently compares its actual contents to the original assignment. This is an agent-to-agent review, not a new user-approval gate. Continue under established authorization when the contract is consistent.

## Specialist: return the exact proposed contract

Save a compact `request-review.json` in the consumer project. Point to existing artifacts instead of duplicating provider history or manufacturing PX2 state for a planning-only task. Its fields are:

- `version`: 1.
- `sources`: the brief and relevant consumer/reference sources, each with project-relative `path`, actual byte `sha256`, and `role`; include locators for the adopted decisions. Numbered locators refer to that individual file, never a concatenated multi-file terminal display. The caller verifies the cited content at those locators. Include the selected `requirements_hash` when PLAR supplied one.
- `request`: `path`, `sha256`, `kind` (`provider_arguments` or `creative_brief`) and the actual tool name when known. Provider arguments must be the complete exact JSON to dispatch, including real reference inputs. Use a creative brief when an operation/schema has not been discovered; do not label it executable.
- `criteria`: `path` and `sha256` for the exact criteria to use. Each criterion has an ID, check, authority/basis, applicable scope and source locator. Distinguish owner/consumer requirements, specialist sample choices, observations and diagnostics.
- `choices`: the consequential specialist choices or unresolved decisions, where each appears in the request/criteria, and its reason. A criterion scoped to a chosen sample can assess that sample; it does not establish a universal project requirement.
- `resume`: existing store/task/output/job links when applicable. Omit absent production state.

Return the packet's path and SHA-256 to the caller. For PX2 production, link the saved request and Q records or an exact exported view with their state/record identity. Do not silently rebuild the request after review. Before dispatch, compare the actual arguments to the reviewed request; reference bytes/handles and non-text controls matter as much as prompt wording.

Keep a required outcome separate from the recipe proposed to achieve it. A qualitative requirement such as matching a reference or conveying a state still needs an acceptance criterion when its palette, geometry, frame count or layout are open. When demoting an unsupported recipe to a sample choice, preserve the underlying required outcome; do not leave only mechanical checks binding. Consumer code establishes its actual data/rendering behavior, not an unmeasured aesthetic quality. Attribute expert quality criteria to expert judgment where that is their basis.

Creative decisions within the assignment need not all go back to the user. For example, choosing a static first sample or a construction method is expert judgment; attributing it to an owner who specified only canvas dimensions is incorrect. Keep the choice explicit and scoped so it can be revised without changing the owner's brief. Observations alone do not become rejection rules.

### Measured facts in creative requests

Do not estimate pixel coordinates by eye and then describe them as verified. When a numerical image fact materially guides a request or verdict, retain the measurement with its source-image hash, frame and coordinate convention. The existing `asset-check --regions COLOR...` / `pixl_asset_check(regions=[...])` measures exact RGBA component boxes; it does not identify the subject or make those colors mandatory. Boxes use zero-based coordinates with exclusive right/bottom edges. For other measurements, save the reproducible calculation. When exact coordinates are unnecessary, describe the visual relationship and supply the actual reference instead.

The caller independently verifies consequential measured claims against the original image and measurement, including the coordinate convention; repeating a specialist's pixel map is not independent verification. Correct unsupported numbers before dispatch while preserving the required visual outcome.

## Resolve source evidence for the comparison

For candidate plans used by selected-asset preparation, call `pixl_request_review`
with the packet path and selected `asset_id` (CLI `request-review PACKET --asset ID
--root PROJECT`). It reads the exact request/criteria identities, returns cited text
with file-local bounds, and includes the current production continuation. It reports
invalid/unresolved locators and changed sources. A resolved excerpt is evidence for
the caller to interpret, not a consistency verdict. Retain this report with the review.

When the connection is already discovered, bind `request.provider` and
`request.connection: {path, sha256}` to its exact artifact. Preparation compares that
reviewed connection with the supplied one; host credentials stay outside the artifact.

Use `lines: [first,last]` on a criterion's source pointer when citing text; retain
`locator` as a human-readable label. Preparation validates explicit bounds before
saving new work. Numbered prose in older plans remains readable and receives
locator diagnostics. For non-text references inspect the actual image/animation;
for named sections resolve the location through the existing source tool. Do not
mark a locator verified merely because its claimed wording appears elsewhere.

Deliberate clean pixel clusters and edges. No fixed palette or binary-alpha restriction. Proposed representative sample before expanding the Working, Retry and Paused family; no approved style reference exists yet.

criteria.scope: Revised representative Ready status sample (queue.ready) for style review before family expansion. Only this candidate's own mechanical, meaning, readability and accent-relationship checks are required at this stage. Family distinction (Working/Retry/Paused vs Ready), renderer integration of statusCell/compactStatus, the style-approval decision and placement at assets/ready-confirmed.png are deferred later-stage obligations recorded in request-review.json and PLAR, not rejection rules for this sample.

2	
3	Read when translating an aesthetic brief into prompts, rejection criteria, or a review. The cases below document observed failure modes; their measured values are not universal pixel-art rules.
4	
5	For delegated work, use the [request and criteria handoff](request-review.md) so the caller can inspect the actual artifacts independently. A self-audit is useful correction work, but its conclusion is not the caller's acceptance.
6	
7	Every production approach carries a compact authority table: property/value, requirement versus observation/proposal, exact source, and applicable scope. Carry the user's requested aesthetic into the derived prompts and checks. An image interpretation that differs from the brief is a reported uncertainty, not permission to replace that treatment. Only established project requirements become production rejection rules; proposals define labeled experiments. A measured color, gap, alpha level, component count or diagnostic contrast result remains an observation until adopted. Before the final handoff, reconcile every enforced restriction in the whole approach with that table; remove unsupported approval claims and keep diagnostic conclusions within their tested conditions.
8	
9	When the brief specifies a treatment, the proposed sample, production instructions and review criteria must all explicitly retain it. For requested selective anti-aliasing and partial transparency, describe where those treatments will be authored and how they will be reviewed; a reference interpretation such as “glow” does not replace either requirement. Uncertainty about a new shape calls for a treatment-preserving experiment, not a default ban on that shape or treatment. When no fixed palette is imposed, production checks omit exact palette membership; a palette experiment remains optional. Describe matching quality, lighting intent and provider reliability as interpretations or untested expectations unless evidence establishes them. A plan or a copied reference recipe cannot guarantee those outcomes.
10	
11	Test each derived restriction against a variation that still satisfies the brief. If that variation could fail the check, the extra restriction is a proposal, not an entailed requirement. Two detached antenna islands, for example, do not forbid another intentional detached detail or require the reference's total component count, coordinates or gap rows. Apply the same scope check to planned failure conclusions: one failed candidate establishes that attempt's failure, not a provider's general inability. A fallback can address that attempt without claiming a universal limit.

For each added restriction, either identify its adopted source or label it as an optional experiment and remove it from production rejection rules. In a proposed experimental prompt, label the extra choices as proposals at the prompt itself. Correct contradictions such as an open alpha policy followed by an unexplained “no antialiasing” directive, or a qualitative color requirement turned into an invented numeric hue threshold. Preserve the earlier draft when revising it and report the scope and any unresolved conflict from this whole-file audit.

# Preserve artistic requirement authority

Read when translating an aesthetic brief into prompts, rejection criteria, or a review. The cases below document observed failure modes; their measured values are not universal pixel-art rules.

For delegated work, use the [request and criteria handoff](request-review.md) so the caller can inspect the actual artifacts independently. A self-audit is useful correction work, but its conclusion is not the caller's acceptance.

Every production approach carries a compact authority table: property/value, requirement versus observation/proposal, exact source, and applicable scope. Carry the user's requested aesthetic into the derived prompts and checks. An image interpretation that differs from the brief is a reported uncertainty, not permission to replace that treatment. Only established project requirements become production rejection rules; proposals define labeled experiments. A measured color, gap, alpha level, component count or diagnostic contrast result remains an observation until adopted. Before the final handoff, reconcile every enforced restriction in the whole approach with that table; remove unsupported approval claims and keep diagnostic conclusions within their tested conditions.

When the brief specifies a treatment, the proposed sample, production instructions and review criteria must all explicitly retain it. For requested selective anti-aliasing and partial transparency, describe where those treatments will be authored and how they will be reviewed; a reference interpretation such as “glow” does not replace either requirement. Uncertainty about a new shape calls for a treatment-preserving experiment, not a default ban on that shape or treatment. When no fixed palette is imposed, production checks omit exact palette membership; a palette experiment remains optional. Describe matching quality, lighting intent and provider reliability as interpretations or untested expectations unless evidence establishes them. A plan or a copied reference recipe cannot guarantee those outcomes.

Test each derived restriction against a variation that still satisfies the brief. If that variation could fail the check, the extra restriction is a proposal, not an entailed requirement. Two detached antenna islands, for example, do not forbid another intentional detached detail or require the reference's total component count, coordinates or gap rows. Apply the same scope check to planned failure conclusions: one failed candidate establishes that attempt's failure, not a provider's general inability. A fallback can address that attempt without claiming a universal limit.

After saving an approach, reopen and read the complete file before the final response. Audit the actual provider prompt, every proposed rejection check and every fallback conclusion against the authority table; reviewing the table or selected sections alone does not complete this step. For each added restriction, either identify its adopted source or label it as an optional experiment and remove it from production rejection rules. In a proposed experimental prompt, label the extra choices as proposals at the prompt itself. Correct contradictions such as an open alpha policy followed by an unexplained “no antialiasing” directive, or a qualitative color requirement turned into an invented numeric hue threshold. Preserve the earlier draft when revising it and report the scope and any unresolved conflict from this whole-file audit.

1	"""Preserve a selected production continuation alongside the agent's own judgments."""
2	
3	import json
4	from hashlib import sha256
5	from pathlib import Path
6	
7	from . import graph, plar, store
8	from .codec import PixlError
9	
10	
11	def save(root, asset_id, requirements_hash, expect, details, path="plar.txt"):
12	    root = Path(root).resolve()
13	    if not isinstance(details, dict) or details.get("status") not in (
14	        "delivered", "partial", "needs_input", "blocked"
15	    ):
16	        raise PixlError("handoff_details", "details needs the agent's assignment status")
17	    if {"resume", "next", "asset_id", "requirements_hash", "version"} & details.keys():
18	        raise PixlError("handoff_details", "Derived fields belong to the snapshot; use caller_actions and future_work for commentary")
19	    selected = plar.read(root, path, asset_id)
20	    if selected["requirements_hash"] != requirements_hash:
21	        raise PixlError("handoff_stale", "Selected requirements changed; reread the asset")
22	    production = selected.get("production") or {}
23	    continuation = production.get("continuation")
24	    if not continuation:
25	        raise PixlError("handoff_state", "No production continuation is available; retain the allocation diagnostic in the ordinary result")
26	    if continuation["state_hash"] != expect:
27	        raise PixlError("handoff_stale", "Production state changed; reread before handing it back")
28	    document = {
29	        "version": 1,
30	        "asset_id": asset_id,
31	        "requirements_hash": requirements_hash,
32	        "resume": continuation,
33	        "next": continuation["action"],
34	        "selection": {
35	            "path": graph.confined(root, path).relative_to(root).as_posix(),
36	            "hash": selected["hash"],
37	            "current": production["selection_current"],
38	        },
39	        "details": details,
40	        "scope": "Snapshot of derived state plus agent-authored observations. No automatic contract, art or delivery acceptance; reread current PLAR before acting.",
41	    }
42	    data = (json.dumps(document, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, indent=2, allow_nan=False) + "\n").encode("utf-8")
43	    digest = sha256(data).hexdigest()
44	    folder = graph.confined(root, ".pixl/handoffs")
45	    with store.lock(folder):
46	        target = graph.confined(root, f".pixl/handoffs/{digest}.json")
47	        if target.exists():
48	            if target.read_bytes() != data:
49	                raise PixlError("handoff_corrupt", "Retained snapshot bytes changed")
50	        else:
51	            store._atomic(target, data)
52	    return {
53	        "path": target.relative_to(root).as_posix(),
54	        "sha256": digest,
55	        "asset_id": asset_id,
56	        "requirements_hash": requirements_hash,
57	        "state_hash": expect,
58	        "next": document["next"],
59	        "scope": document["scope"],
60	    }

87	Cold resumption uses the retained inspection report to recover the exact old inputs,
88	criterion text, declared viewing limits and next action. Continue through
89	[sample acceptance](intake-sample.md) or [family production](family-delivery.md) as
90	appropriate. Successful publication verifies retention, not whether a host truly
91	looked or an engine accepted the asset.

1	# Agent-to-agent asset work
2	
3	Use this operation when a calling Claude/Codex agent assigns visual work to PIXL. PIXL is the callable name of pixel-lab-agent (PLA). The profile supplies artistic judgment; this contract carries the assignment and result between agents.
4	
5	## Caller → specialist
6	
7	Supply the smallest complete assignment:
8	
9	| Context | What the specialist needs |
10	| --- | --- |
11	| Outcome | Asset purpose, requested files and relevant success criteria |
12	| Workspace | Absolute consumer root; installed PIXL skill location |
13	| Requirements | Selected PLAR asset packet, or a complete direct brief |
14	| References | Addressable files/owned resource IDs, their roles and what to preserve |
15	| Authority | User decisions, proposals, unresolved choices and established authorization/limits |
16	| Resume | Existing store/task/output and pending provider IDs, when present |
17	| Integration | Destination, relevant consumers, and authorized code/import work |
18	
19	Keep generated assets, request/review artifacts, helper scripts and scratch/previews inside the assigned consumer root unless the assignment names another authorized destination. Resolve paths against that root through each delegation and resumption; the shell's current directory or the kit's installation directory is not an implicit output destination. The caller checks returned paths against the agreed workspace as well as checking their bytes.
20	
21	For PLAR, call `pixl_plar_read` with `asset_id`. Pass its selected row, transitive dependencies, source bindings, visual references and `requirements_hash`. Queue summaries alone omit production context. The reader supplies absolute paths for this filesystem; if the delegate uses another workspace, rebase paths and verify the same source bytes there.
22	
23	The caller delegates to the native PIXL agent or a native specialist loading the shared PIXL skill. Keep the caller's model/tool/permission settings unless the assignment requires otherwise. Include the actual assignment in the delegation; naming a skill or saying “make the assets” does not transfer the parent's conversation. Credentials stay in the host's PixelLab connection.
24	
25	A direct brief can proceed without first manufacturing a PLAR document. Use PLAR when allocation, dependencies or ongoing project work benefit from it. The caller owns application-wide priorities; PIXL owns art direction, appropriate PixelLab operation selection, reference use and visual evaluation within the assignment.
26	
27	## Specialist → caller while working
28	
29	Read the actual reference and consumer context. Resolve facts from supplied files and tools before asking the caller. If one consequential choice remains, send a small question with the affected asset, alternatives and what it unlocks. The caller can answer from its context or relay to the user. Continue unaffected work, carrying existing authorization rather than re-requesting it.
30	
31	Keep creative proposals explicit. Distinguish “the reference contains this” from “the user requires this.” Report a tool/input mismatch with the viable path, not an invented parameter or a silently changed asset size. Progress messages report actual saved plans, job IDs or inspected files.
32	
33	Resume the same task/state where possible. Check retained provider attempts before another request. A failed or interrupted child is a handoff boundary; it is not permission for the parent to duplicate a potentially submitted generation.
34	
35	Before adopting a proposed production contract, use the [request and criteria handoff](request-review.md). The specialist returns exact source/request/criteria artifacts; the caller reads them independently and records a source-grounded comparison. Preserve specialist choices as choices, and continue within existing authorization once discrepancies are resolved.
36	
37	## Specialist → caller at completion
38	
39	Return a compact structured result (JSON or equivalent named fields):
40	
41	- `status`: `delivered`, `partial`, `needs_input`, or `blocked`, judged against this assignment.
42	- `asset_id` and `requirements_hash` when PLAR supplied them; direct-brief tasks identify their brief.
43	- `artifacts`: project-relative paths, role, actual hashes and dimensions/frame metadata as relevant.
44	- `checks`: actual mechanical, visual and integration findings, with evidence paths and unavailable checks.
45	- `request_review`: packet and caller-review paths/hashes, with unresolved findings when applicable.
46	- `provider`: observed resource/job IDs and the production-state location needed to resume.
47	- `questions` or `next`: only outstanding decisions and the next concrete action.
48	
49	When durable production state is in use, finish its accepted-candidate selection and task state through `task-complete` / `pixl_task_complete` after the saved required checks pass. The caller reads `workflow` to confirm the completed state agrees with the delivered files; an open task remains an explicit unfinished part of the operation. A planning-only assignment does not need manufactured production state.
50	
51	Judge completion against the delegated scope. A planning-only assignment is delivered when its complete reviewed contract is returned; future generation remains outside that scope. An assignment ending at an accepted request is delivered when that request and its resumable state are returned, while the asset remains unaccepted and its production task open. State both facts explicitly. A full asset-production assignment is still partial at contract handoff. Retain the provider connection and simulated/live provenance with every job ID and next action; an ID cannot be resumed on a different service.
52	
53	Include only applicable fields. A generation-only task can deliver a reviewed artifact while explicitly leaving engine import unverified. If the assignment requires integration, unavailable integration keeps that part unfinished. Never use a provider's completed status as artistic acceptance.
54	
55	The caller opens the returned files and checks the relevant result against its original assignment. Compare a fresh selected PLAR packet if source context changed. `requirements_hash` tracks the selected requirements, reference bytes and dependency requirements; status/next-action changes alone do not change it. It is neither a spend authorization nor a readiness verdict. The existing file `hash` still governs PLAR writes.
56	
57	For a PLAR-bound result, reread the selected asset after the last state change, then
58	use `pixl_plar_handoff` with its `asset_id`, `requirements_hash`, production `hash` as
59	`expect`, and your `details` object. CLI: `plar handoff DETAILS_JSON --asset ID
60	--requirements HASH --expect STATE_HASH --root PROJECT`. The operation saves the
61	complete derived continuation and immediate `next` unchanged in an immutable file.
62	Return that file's path/hash as `handoff`; the caller opens it and compares its state
63	identity with fresh focused PLAR. Do not copy selected fields into a rewritten resume.
64	Older handoffs remain readable; their original bytes are not migrated or relabelled.
65	
66	`details` contains your assignment status, delivered artifacts, request-review links,
67	expert reasoning, actual checks, unresolved issues and future work. Keep completed
68	caller actions with evidence in `details.caller_actions`, and subsequent goals in
69	`details.future_work`. A completed caller review can be reported there while the
70	runtime still derives `review_delivery`; it does not replace that derived action.
71	The snapshot records both facts without inventing a new acceptance event. The runtime
72	does not decide whether your artistic judgment or assignment-status claim is correct.
73	
74	On a cold resume, read the saved handoff and current focused PLAR. Changed state or
75	requirements require a fresh snapshot; matching hashes preserve the original job and
76	its originating connection. Resolve pending work, then retrieve/import and review its
77	actual result before proposing another generation. The caller's normal response can
78	explain later work in prose while linking the exact resumable artifact.
79	
80	Keep detailed receipts in project files so the caller receives useful art and decisions rather than an entire transcript or image encoded in text.

content.content: {"id":"silhouette-readability","title":"Evaluate identity using silhouette and target backgrounds","applies_to":["characters","inventory icons","interactive props"],"requires":["Intended viewing scale, representative backgrounds and identity landmarks","Applicability judgment: the cited cluster constraints, temporal-change discussion and UI brief support feature preservation and contextual clarity; they do not prescribe the flat-mask or multi-background procedure below."],"procedure":["Treat this inspection sequence as a curated expert diagnostic proposal. Select the views that answer the current asset question; do not attribute the sequence itself to the cited passages or make it an owner requirement.","Render a flat opaque mask before detailing.","Inspect major proportions, negative spaces and landmark separation at native logical scale.","Compare the colored asset on representative light, dark and busy backgrounds."],"checks":["Named identity landmarks remain visible at the target size.","Required gaps stay open and interactive forms separate from their surroundings."],"pitfalls":["Silhouette alone cannot validate faces, materials or fine symbols.","No contrast ratio or component count proves aesthetic quality.","The cited temporal silhouette-change condition is animation-specific; it does not impose a static-icon construction rule. The key fixture proves its landmark checks only, not universal aesthetic validity."],"sources":[{"path":"training/original-docs/PIXEL-ART-DEEP-RESEARCH.md","start":857,"end":867},{"path":"training/original-docs/PIXEL-ART-DEEP-RESEARCH.md","start":1563,"end":1573},{"path":"training/original-docs/PIXEL-ART-ASSETS.md","start":11,"end":15}],"poc":{"kind":"visual-review-fixture","procedure":["Draw a 16x16 key with a ring hole, shaft and two teeth; render mask and colored views on three backgrounds.","Create a negative example by filling the hole and merging the teeth."],"acceptance":["Record native-scale contact sheets and explicit pass/fail for hole, shaft and both teeth.","Negative example fails the landmark checklist; aesthetic review remains separate."]}}

{"id":"edge-rhythm","title":"Audit stair-step runs without imposing one contour style","applies_to":["clean linework","small curved forms","hard silhouettes"],"requires":["A contour mask and declared intentional corners or irregular regions"],"procedure":["Trace boundary runs and highlight sudden run-length changes.","Regularize only contours intended to read as smooth.","Preserve corners, damage and organic asymmetry identified in the brief."],"checks":["A supplied straight diagonal retains its declared repeating step pattern.","No protected corner changes during cleanup."],"pitfalls":["Not every uneven run is a jaggy; shape can require an abrupt change.","Mechanical contour smoothing can erase style and identity."],"sources":[{"path":"training/original-docs/PIXEL-ART-DEEP-RESEARCH.md","start":1402,"end":1431},{"path":"training/original-docs/PIXEL-ART-DEEP-RESEARCH.md","start":857,"end":867}],"poc":{"kind":"raster-fixture","procedure":["Use an 8x8 45-degree one-pixel staircase and record its unit step sequence.","Add a one-cell horizontal detour at the midpoint; mark it first accidental, then intentional."],"acceptance":["Detour is reported in both cases with its location.","Only the accidental case is eligible for correction."]}}

{"id":"integer-presentation","title":"Render at a declared logical grid and inspect device pixels","applies_to":["strict-grid games","pixel previews","sprite delivery"],"requires":["Logical resolution, camera convention and target viewport dimensions"],"procedure":["Render or sample at the logical grid, then use a declared integer scale where required.","Apply nearest sampling to image scaling and account for browser device pixel ratio.","Inspect the final output, not only a CSS property or import setting."],"checks":["A logical pixel expands into a uniform scale-by-scale block in the fixture.","No new colors appear during opaque nearest-neighbor enlargement."],"pitfalls":["Nearest filtering alone does not constrain lighting resolution.","Noninteger scaling, arbitrary rotation and browser zoom can change displayed pixel widths."],"sources":[{"path":"training/original-docs/PIXEL-ART-DEEP-RESEARCH.md","start":907,"end":919},{"path":"training/original-docs/PIXEL-ART-DEEP-RESEARCH.md","start":1293,"end":1315},{"path":"training/original-docs/PIXEL-ART-DEEP-RESEARCH.md","start":1636,"end":1638}],"poc":{"kind":"raster-fixture","procedure":["Scale a 2x2 image of four opaque distinct colors by 3 to 6x6.","Inspect every 3x3 quadrant and compare palette membership."],"acceptance":["Each quadrant is exactly uniform and matches its source pixel.","The final image contains exactly four colors."]}}

{"id":"alpha-contract","title":"Declare alpha and compositing behavior","applies_to":["transparent sprites","glows","sprite atlases"],"requires":["RGBA interpretation, straight or premultiplied alpha, and allowed alpha levels"],"procedure":["Keep alpha policy separate from RGB palette membership.","Use the chosen compositing equation consistently through export, import and display.","Inspect edges against light and dark backgrounds after round-trip import."],"checks":["Binary-alpha assets contain only 0 and 255 unless an exception is declared.","Composited fixtures agree with the declared alpha model."],"pitfalls":["Fully transparent RGB channels can differ without changing visible appearance.","Multiplying premultiplied RGB by alpha again darkens edges."],"sources":[{"path":"training/original-docs/PIXEL-ART-DEEP-RESEARCH.md","start":945,"end":977},{"path":"training/original-docs/PIXEL-ART-DEEP-RESEARCH.md","start":1276,"end":1291},{"path":"training/original-docs/PIXEL-ART-ASSETS.md","start":942,"end":958}],"poc":{"kind":"compositing-fixture","procedure":["For straight alpha composite red (255,0,0,0.5) over blue (0,0,255) in a declared linear numeric fixture.","Separately validate binary-alpha pixels [0,255,127]."],"acceptance":["Unrounded linear result is (127.5,0,127.5).","Binary-alpha validation reports only the 127 entry; display color-space conversion is a separate step."]}}

{"id":"semantic-clusters","title":"Track raster connectivity and semantic clusters separately","applies_to":["sprite cleanup","protected eyes","material boundaries","micro-animation"],"requires":["A declared 4- or 8-neighbor rule and semantic masks"],"procedure":["Extract same-color connected components with the selected rule.","Label intentional details such as eyes, sparks and stars; these may be legal singletons.","Use semantic masks across multiple colors when a feature must be edited as a unit."],"checks":["Connected-component counts are reproducible.","Protected feature masks remain present after operations."],"pitfalls":["A semantic cluster need not be a single-color connected component.","Automatically deleting every singleton destroys legitimate detail."],"sources":[{"path":"training/original-docs/PIXEL-ART-DEEP-RESEARCH.md","start":1402,"end":1445},{"path":"training/original-docs/PIXEL-ART-DEEP-RESEARCH.md","start":857,"end":867}],"poc":{"kind":"raster-fixture","procedure":["Create an 8x8 image with a 2x2 body, two diagonal pixels and one isolated protected eye.","Run 4- and 8-neighbor component extraction; then delete the protected eye in a mutant."],"acceptance":["The diagonal pair is separate under 4-connectivity and joined under 8-connectivity.","Only the mutant fails feature preservation."]}}

{"id":"state-driven-pixel-ui","title":"Tie pixel UI animation to actual state and input","applies_to":["pixel interaction prompts","health icons","selected project UI"],"requires":["Authoritative input or gameplay state and project-specific styling brief"],"procedure":["Map idle, pressed, disabled and health states to explicit visual states.","Use timing only for the transition the real event triggered.","Retain static recognizability and adapt scale and color across the surrounding UI."],"checks":["The visual state corresponds to the supplied input or health state.","No decorative timer reports an event or progress that has not occurred."],"pitfalls":["The archive's keyboard prompt and Waylight palette rules belong to its original project.","A CSS demo with blur or continuous motion may conflict with a strict-grid asset profile."],"sources":[{"path":"training/original-docs/PIXEL-ART-ASSETS.md","start":9,"end":17},{"path":"training/original-docs/PIXEL-ART-ASSETS.md","start":916,"end":960},{"path":"training/original-docs/PIXEL-ART-ASSETS.md","start":11450,"end":11458}],"poc":{"kind":"state-fixture","procedure":["For an original 8x8 interaction icon define idle, pressed and disabled masks.","Feed enabled/down/up/disabled/down events and record selected state."],"acceptance":["States are idle,pressed,idle,disabled,disabled.","Disabled input does not produce a pressed-success visual; source styling is not globally imposed."]}}

{"id":"frame-timing","title":"Author duration and event semantics per frame","applies_to":["sprite animation","attacks","idle loops","UI feedback"],"requires":["Ordered frame IDs, positive durations and loop or one-shot policy"],"procedure":["Store durations explicitly rather than assuming uniform FPS.","Name anticipation, action, impact and settle events where relevant.","Define half-open time intervals so event and frame boundaries have no ambiguity."],"checks":["Every duration is positive and playback reaches the expected frame at boundary times.","One-shot terminal states and looping wrap behavior are explicit."],"pitfalls":["More frames do not automatically improve weight or readability.","Unspecified preview FPS must not overwrite authored durations."],"sources":[{"path":"training/original-docs/PIXEL-ART-DEEP-RESEARCH.md","start":869,"end":905},{"path":"training/original-docs/PIXEL-ART-ASSETS.md","start":948,"end":960}],"poc":{"kind":"timeline-fixture","procedure":["Use frames A,B,C with durations 80,40,120 milliseconds and a looping total of 240.","Sample t=0,79,80,119,120,239,240 using half-open intervals."],"acceptance":["Frame IDs are A,A,B,B,C,C,A.","An impact event at 120 fires once per loop crossing."]}}
